title: The Secret Coach Pochettino Used to Wake Up a Sleepy U.S. Soccer Team
summary: Imagine you’re on a soccer team, but some players don’t seem to care if they win or lose. That’s what Coach Mauricio Pochettino found when he took over the U.S. men’s national team in 2024. He was shocked. In his home country of Argentina, players treat every game like the World Cup final. But here, many regulars were too comfortable. Pochettino knew he had to change that fast, with the 2026 World Cup coming up on home soil. So he did something bold. Over 18 months, he invited more than 70 players to try out. He told everyone, no matter how famous, they had to earn their spot. Some big names, like star winger Christian Pulisic, even got left off a tournament roster after a disagreement. At first, it looked like a disaster. The team lost to Panama, Canada, Turkey, and got crushed 0-4 by Switzerland. Fans worried. But Pochettino kept saying it was like an ant’s work—tiny steps that add up. And guess what? It worked. The U.S. just won their World Cup group and now have a smoother path in the knockout rounds, starting Wednesday against Bosnia and Herzegovina in Santa Clara, California. Pochettino, who once coached superstars like Lionel Messi and Kylian Mbappé, took a job many saw as a step down. But he turned a sleepy giant into a team of believers. “It’s hard work and slow work,” he said. “The work of an ant, little step, little step.” Those little steps might just lead to something huge.
why_it_matters: Just like practicing a sport a little bit every day, this story shows that small, patient steps can turn a struggling group into a winning team.

In 2026, the United States, Canada, and Mexico will host the World Cup together, which makes home-field advantage extra exciting.
Mauricio Pochettino (a famous coach from Argentina) used to lead top clubs like Tottenham Hotspur and Paris Saint-Germain, where he coached stars like Kylian Mbappé.
Article_Structure: WHO: Coach Mauricio Pochettino and the U.S. men's national soccer team
WHAT: He held tryouts for over 70 players and benched big names to build a tougher team, which just won their World Cup group
WHERE: United States; next game in Santa Clara, California
